memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "For I know how rebellious and stiff-necked you are. If you have been rebellious against the Lord while I am still alive and with you, how much more will you rebel after I die! Assemble before me all the elders of your tribes and all your officials, so that I can speak these words in their hearing and call the heavens and the earth to testify against them." — Deut 31:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses speaks with unflinching honesty about the people: "I know how rebellious and stiff-necked you are." He had led them for forty years and knew their hearts well — their tendency to grumble, to wander, to resist God. He harbours no illusions. Even while he was still with them, they had rebelled; how much more would they after he was gone? It is a sobering, realistic assessment of the human heart.

This honesty is actually a gift. Scripture never flatters us or pretends we are better than we are. It tells us the truth: our hearts are prone to wander, quick to rebel, "stiff-necked" and resistant to God. We might find this uncomfortable, but facing the truth about ourselves is the beginning of real change. We cannot be helped where we will not be honest.

And here is the wonder: God knows all of this about us, and loves us still. He is not shocked by our rebellion, not caught off guard by our failures. He sees the stiff-necked heart clearly — and He set His love on us anyway.

This is precisely why we need more than good advice or a good example; we need a new heart and a Saviour. God promised to deal with our stubborn hearts by His Spirit (Ezek 36:26), and He accomplished it through Christ, who died for rebels like us. The honest diagnosis of our condition only makes the remedy more glorious. Bring your stiff-necked heart to the God who knows it fully and loves you completely.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I honest with God about the rebellion and stubbornness in my own heart?
2. How does it comfort me that God knows my heart fully and loves me still?
3. What "stiff-necked" area do I need to bring to God for change?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You know my heart — its wandering, its stubbornness, its rebellion — and You love me still. Thank You for the new heart You give in Christ. Soften my stiff-necked heart and draw me close. Amen.
